data.narrative:
Neura Robotics, a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Reger, has raised $1.4B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, including Series B and D stage companies such as Exotec ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), and Hadrian ($1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using $1.4B total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implies a valuation of $2.4B. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector comparables at matching or adjacent stages yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The two methods diverge notably, reflecting uncertainty around growth trajectory and peer heterogeneity.

Synthesizing both approaches yields a triangulated range of $1.4B (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $2.0B. The $600M spread reflects material uncertainty around whether Neura will achieve typical stage-progression multiples or track closer to current peer medians. Key variables driving outcomes include commercialization velocity relative to peer set, capital efficiency through Series C, and market-timing factors affecting robotics valuations.
